title: Stirling-type lower bound for a factorial ratio
statement:
Let $a,b,n\in\bbn$ with $a>0$, $b>0$, and $a+b=n$, and let $c>0$ be a real number. Suppose the factorial product $a!\,b!$ admits the Stirling-type upper bound
\[
a!\,b! \;\le\; c\cdot\Bigl(\sqrt{2}\,\sqrt{a}\,\sqrt{\pi}\,(a/e)^{a}\Bigr)\Bigl(\sqrt{2}\,\sqrt{b}\,\sqrt{\pi}\,(b/e)^{b}\Bigr).
\]
Then the ratio $n!/(a!\,b!)$ is bounded below by
\[
\frac{n^{n}}{a^{a}\,b^{b}}\cdot\frac{1}{c\,\sqrt{\pi/2}\,\sqrt{n}}
\;\le\;
\frac{n!}{a!\,b!}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: Stirling-type upper bound on a!·b! with constant c
replaced:
Let $a,b,n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $a,b>0$, $a+b=n$, and let $c>0$. Suppose the Stirling-type bound
\[
a!\,\cdot\,b! \;\le\; c\cdot\Big(\sqrt{2}\sqrt{a}\sqrt{\pi}\,(a/e)^a\cdot\sqrt{2}\sqrt{b}\sqrt{\pi}\,(b/e)^b\Big)
\]
holds. Then
\[
\frac{n^n}{a^a\,b^b}\,\Big/\,\big(c\,\sqrt{\pi/2}\,\sqrt{n}\big)
\;\le\;
\frac{n!}{a!\,b!}.
\]
